paper_title: Performance and Thermal Tradeoffs for Energy-Efficient Monolithic 3D Network-on-Chip

scenario.figure_or_table: Figure 15 (with Table 1 on PDF page 14 and Table 2 on PDF page 14)
scenario.description: Comparison of maximum, average and minimum chip temperatures for the four-layer PTO TSV-based and PTM M3D-based 3D small-world NoC designs with static VFI power management. The paper reports M3D peak temperature up to 29.1% (average 20.1%) lower than TSV. The average max-min temperature difference is 16.7 C for TSV and 2.9 C for M3D. Thermal profiles come from HotSpot, and the optimizer uses the Cong et al. resistive-network temperature model inside simulated annealing. No per-block coordinates or power values are published in the paper text. No code, data or repository links were found in the paper.
scenario.architecture: 64-core four-layer 3D small-world NoC manycore chip (10 mm x 10 mm per layer, 4x4x4 grid), TSV-based (PTO) versus monolithic 3D (PTM, multi-tier routers, MIVs, thin ILD), with four static voltage-frequency islands
scenario.workload: Eight benchmarks run in GEM5 with McPAT power: SPLASH-2 (FFT, RADIX, LU, WATER) and PARSEC (DEDUP, VIPS, FLUIDANIMATE, CANNEAL)
scenario.operating_point: Static VFI cluster sizes and V/F levels per benchmark (Table 1, PDF page 14); results reported as maximum, average and minimum chip temperature in degrees Celsius, with a 110 C throttling limit (PDF page 17)

original_setup.solver: HotSpot (Huang et al. 2006) for thermal profiles of the whole system, with a fast Cong et al. 2004 3D resistive-network model (vertical and horizontal heat flow, Eqs. 3-4) inside the optimization loop. Performance and power come from GEM5 with McPAT.
original_setup.optimizer: Simulated annealing on the joint cost = alpha*O + beta*T (Eq. 2) with two moves, VFI-constrained core swapping S'(i,j) and new-link placement L(l), each chosen with probability 0.5. The M3D variant (PTM) uses altered cost-function weights, and the TSV variant is PTO.
original_setup.controller: Static voltage-frequency islanding (SVFI) with four heterogeneous VFI clusters and per-benchmark static V/F levels (Table 1, PDF page 14). No dynamic controller is used. The 110 C thermal-throttling limit is not triggered.
original_setup.benchmark: Scenario: four-layer 64-core 3D small-world NoC (10 mm x 10 mm per layer, 4x4x4 grid), PTO TSV vs PTM M3D with static VFI (Figure 15, PDF page 20). Workloads are SPLASH-2 (FFT, RADIX, LU, WATER) and PARSEC (DEDUP, VIPS, FLUID, CAN), with GEM5 (64 cores, MOESI_CMP_directory, 64KB L1, 8MB shared L2) and ALASH routing.

thermal_observable.unit: percent reduction in peak temperature (M3D PTM vs TSV PTO); the paper also reports temperatures in degrees C, with an average max-min difference of 16.7 C (TSV) and 2.9 C (M3D)
thermal_observable.location: Maximum, average and minimum chip temperature over the four-layer 64-core manycore chip from HotSpot, plotted per benchmark in Figure 15
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum over benchmarks of the per-benchmark peak-temperature reduction (up to 29.1%, average 20.1% over benchmarks). Absolute per-benchmark temperatures exist only in the Figure 15 bar chart and are not tabulated in the text.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper models a 4-tier 3D stack (TSV with BCB bonding layers versus monolithic ILD with MIVs), which a 2D steady-state Studio runner cannot represent, so inter-tier thermal resistance and the TSV/M3D difference are lost.

The M3D versus TSV result depends on vertical thermal resistance (R_j, R_b) and layer material differences extracted from HotSpot. These parameters are not published in the paper, so they cannot be reproduced.

The study is a multi-core NoC (cores, routers, links, VFI clusters) with architecture-level placement optimization. The paper publishes no per-block geometry, coordinates or power values, so no complete floorplan or power table exists.

The optimizer is simulated annealing over NoC core, router and link placement with a joint performance-temperature cost, while a Studio thermal runner would use a different or no optimizer. The optimizer is therefore not replicated.
The workload power comes from GEM5/McPAT per benchmark with static VFI voltage-frequency levels. These powers are not published, and no controller or time series is available.

The cooling and heat-sink boundary conditions, package and interposer model are not specified in the paper, though the heat sink location is described qualitatively (high-power VFI clusters near the sink).

No transient behavior, reliability analysis (e.g., NBTI, mentioned only qualitatively) or throttling dynamics are simulated. The paper reports steady-style max/avg/min temperatures with no throttling triggered.

missing_inputs: No linked code, data, repository or supplementary assets; the packet's artifact search found no links and the assets list is empty.

Per-block x_m, y_m, width_m, height_m: no floorplan coordinates published for cores, routers or VFI clusters. Only layer sizes are given (Table 2, PDF page 14: 10x10 mm for four layers) and a 4x4x4 grid on PDF page 13.
Per-block power_rows (name and watts): no per-core, per-router or total chip power values published. McPAT outputs are not reported.
Absolute per-benchmark temperature values for Figure 15 are only in a bar chart; no tabulated values (would require digitization with uncertainty).
HotSpot configuration, material properties, layer thicknesses, thermal resistances R_j and R_b, heat-sink and ambient boundary conditions for TSV and M3D stacks.
Final optimized placements of cores, VFI clusters and multi-tier routers for PTO TSV and PTM M3D, and the alpha and beta cost weights.
Studio package/material assumptions cannot be tied to the paper; none are recorded. No complete experiment exists, so the floorplan is empty.
